# Reporting and Interpretation {.unnumbered}

A reader should be able to identify what was analysed, how the result was obtained, how large the estimate was, and how uncertain it remains. Reporting therefore starts with the question and method, followed by a result that retains the denominator, units, reference categories, and relevant uncertainty.

The reporting chapter brings together the preceding analyses. It explains the functions of a results paragraph, a table, a figure, and a methods statement. It also addresses common errors such as copying an entire software output, presenting only p-values, describing association as causation, and interpreting a non-significant result as absence of an effect.

The SAMPL guidelines provide a general basis for statistical reporting in biomedical manuscripts. Study-specific reporting guidance should also be selected according to the design; STROBE applies to the observational designs listed in its statement. [@SAMPL; @STROBE]

By the end of this part, the reader should be able to produce a concise results section that another researcher can interpret and assess without access to the jamovi output window.
